children: BJ's Wholesale Club raised its outlook for the year on the back of higher profit and revenue in the recent quarter, as well as accelerating same-store sales.
The warehouse club chain on Friday said it now expects adjusted earnings of $5.10 to $5.30 a share, up from a prior outlook of $4.60 to $4.80 a share.
The company also raised the low end of its forecast for comparable-club sales excluding gasoline to up 2.5% from up 2%, while maintaining the high end at up 3%.
Analysts are looking for adjusted earnings of $4.74 a share and comparable-club sales growth of 2.6%, according to FactSet.
The higher outlook came as BJ's delivered what Chief Executive Bob Eddy called a strong third quarter, driven by both traffic and membership growth.

"We seized a unique opportunity to invest in our stakeholders," he said. "We're excited about the momentum across our strategic priorities, and we remain committed to investing in growth for the long term."
BJ's reported a profit of $219.5 million, or $1.73 a share, for its quarter ended Oct. 31, compared with $152.1 million, or $1.15 a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out one-time items, earnings still came in at $1.73 a share. Analysts had expected adjusted earnings of $1.26 a share.
Total revenues jumped 17% to $6.28 billion, topping Wall Street models for $5.97 billion.
Comparable-club sales, which account for store openings and closings, increased by 14%, or by 4.1% excluding gasoline sales. Analysts were looking for a 2.7% gain.
